transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello. It's nice to meet you too. 

Well, I suppose what brought me in is that I keep finding myself checking things over and over again. It's mostly the same boxes, my day-to-day lists, and the drawers around our condo. I'll check them repeatedly before I can finally move on to whatever I'm supposed to be doing. 

The frustrating part is that I know perfectly well I already looked. But I still do it, even when my wife is just standing there waiting for me to leave it be so we can leave the house. I just figured it was time I came in and talked to someone about it.
When you feel the need to check again, is it because an unwanted thought or urge suddenly pops into your mind that you might have missed something?

Yes, that is pretty much exactly what happens. I keep getting these... well, these nagging thoughts. 

I'll suddenly worry that I might have accidentally thrown away something important from my old teaching files, or maybe that I put a needed tool in the wrong box. And I know better. I tell myself it's highly unlikely I did that, but the thought just keeps coming back anyway. It just makes it really hard to sit down and settle until I go look again.
When those nagging thoughts come up, do they feel like your own thoughts, even though they seem unreasonable?

Well, yes, I suppose they do. I mean... they're definitely coming from my own head. It's not like I'm hearing voices or someone else is putting them there, if that's what you mean. It's just my own mind, second-guessing myself, even when I know better.
When these thoughts come up, do you try to resist them?

I do try, yes. Like I mentioned a moment ago with those worries about my old teaching files or the tools... I try to tell myself it's unlikely and just ignore it. I'll try to just sit there and read or watch television, or whatever it is I'm doing. 

But... well, no matter how much I try to push it away, the thought just keeps coming back anyway. It just nags at me, and it makes it so hard to actually settle down until I finally give in and go check the box.
Do you ever feel you have to arrange things until they seem exactly right?

No, I don't really have that issue. I mean, I like things to be tidy, but I don't feel any sort of... compulsion to arrange things until they're perfect. It's really just the checking that bothers me.
On a typical day, about how much total time do you spend checking these boxes, lists, or drawers?

Well, it adds up, I suppose. I don't know the exact minutes, but it's enough that... well, unpacking the condo has taken much longer than it really should have. And I've been putting off preparing for my volunteer tutoring at the library, and even my hobbies. I just feel like I can't move on to those things until I've verified everything enough times.
Do these checking habits feel upsetting and unwanted to you?

Yes, they do. I mean, I really don't want to be doing this. It's frustrating. I just want to unpack and enjoy my retirement, but these thoughts keep getting in the way. It's definitely upsetting to feel like I can't just let it go.
Do these checking rituals take more than an hour of your day in total?

I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I haven't really looked at a clock while I'm doing it. It might add up to an hour if you put all those little moments together, or... well, maybe it's a bit less. I just know it's enough to get in the way of my day, but I really couldn't give you a precise amount of time.
Do those unwanted thoughts ever come up even when you are not checking or about to check something?

Yes, they do. Um, I could just be sitting down, not doing anything, and I keep getting these nagging thoughts. I'll start worrying that I might have thrown away something important from my old teaching files, or... or maybe I put a needed tool in the wrong box while I was unpacking. And even when I tell myself it's really unlikely that I did that, the thought just comes back. It makes it very hard to just settle and relax.
Do you feel that these repeated thoughts and checking are excessive or unreasonable?

Yes, I do. Honestly, that's what brought me in to see you. I know it's unreasonable because... well, I find myself checking the same boxes, my lists, the drawers here in the condo over and over before I can just move on to the next thing. And the frustrating part is, I know perfectly well I already looked. My wife will be right there, waiting for me to just leave it be so we can go do something, and I still feel stuck doing it. So, yes, I definitely know it's excessive.
If you had to estimate, do these checking rituals take more than an hour a day in total?

Well, like I mentioned just a moment ago, it's really hard to say for sure. If I absolutely had to guess, I suppose it could be right around an hour altogether. But I really haven't timed myself. It's just spread out in little chunks throughout the day, so I honestly can't give you a better estimate than what I said before.
Besides the checking itself, do you have repeated unwanted thoughts that intrude into your mind and make you anxious?

Well, like I was saying earlier... yes, I do get those thoughts. They just pop into my head out of nowhere, even when I'm just sitting around. I start worrying about throwing away old files or misplacing tools, and it definitely makes me feel anxious and on edge. I can't seem to just shake them off, no matter how much I try to tell myself it's fine.
Which bothers you more: the unwanted thoughts themselves, or the checking you do to relieve them?

Hmm... I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't thought about it quite like that. I suppose... well, they just kind of go together. The thoughts are what make me anxious in the first place, but then feeling stuck doing the checking is incredibly frustrating. So, I don't know if I can really pick one that bothers me more than the other.
Do these checking habits feel like they fit with the kind of person you are, or do they feel alien and not like you?

I'm not really sure how to answer that. I haven't ever stopped to think about it in those terms. I mean... I've always been a fairly careful person, I suppose. But "alien" is a strong word. It's just... well, it's just something I find myself doing now, even when I'd rather be doing something else. So I really couldn't say if it feels like me or not.
Have there been times when these unwanted thoughts kept bothering you but you did not do any checking in response?

No, I... I don't believe so. If the thought starts bothering me, I pretty much always end up checking. I can't really recall a time where I just sat there and let it bother me without doing anything about it. It's just... well, I just go check so I can put it out of my mind.
If you had to choose, which is more distressing for you: the intrusive thoughts, or the checking rituals?

Well, like I was just saying a moment ago... it's awfully hard to separate them. Even if I really had to choose, I'm not sure I could give you a straight answer. 

The thoughts start the worry, and the checking is the chore I have to do to fix it. They just go hand in hand for me. So neither one really stands out as being worse than the other. I just don't think I can pick one.
When you cannot check right away, do the thoughts themselves feel very distressing?

Yes, they do. I keep getting these... these nagging thoughts that I might have thrown away something important from my old teaching files, or maybe that I put a needed tool in the wrong box. 

If I can't go look right then, it just eats at me. Even when I sit there and tell myself it's highly unlikely I did anything of the sort, the thought just comes right back. It makes it very hard to settle down and focus on anything else until I can get up and check. So, yes, the thoughts themselves are quite bothersome.
Do you wish these thoughts and checking would stop?

Yes, I certainly do. It's... well, it's just a nuisance, really. I'm retired now, and I'd much rather spend my day relaxing or doing things I enjoy, instead of having to get up and check on old files or tools just to get some peace of mind. So, yes, I'd be quite happy if the whole thing just went away.
Do these unwanted thoughts ever come into your mind at times when you are not doing, and not about to do, any checking?

Yes, they do. Like I was mentioning a few minutes ago, they can really just pop up out of nowhere. 

I might just be sitting in my armchair trying to read a book, nowhere near my desk or the garage, and suddenly I get that nagging feeling all over again. I'll start worrying that I might have accidentally tossed out an important paper from my old teaching files, or maybe put a tool in the wrong box. And even when I sit there and try to reason with myself, knowing it's highly unlikely I actually did that, the thought just keeps coming back. It makes it awfully hard to just settle down and enjoy my afternoon. So, yes, they definitely happen even when I'm not actively doing or planning to do any checking.
Would you say the unwanted thoughts are a major problem for you in their own right?

Well, yes, I would. Like I was just saying, it's... it's those nagging thoughts themselves that really get to me. I know I keep mentioning the old teaching files and the tools, but that's exactly what it is. I'll get it in my head that I threw something important away or put a needed tool in the wrong box, and even when I tell myself it's highly unlikely I did any such thing, the thought just comes right back. It just sits there and makes it so hard to settle down and relax. So, yes, even without the checking part, just having those thoughts stuck in my head is a problem all on its own.

While this relates to the overall distress of OCD, it does not specifically ask for the manifestation of the obsessions, compulsions, or the functional impairment itself, but rather the patient's attitude toward having the condition.

patient.answer: Yes, I certainly do. It's... well, it's just a nuisance, really. I'm retired now, and I'd much rather spend my day relaxing or doing things I enjoy, instead of having to get up and check on old files or tools just to get some peace of mind. So, yes, I'd be quite happy if the whole thing just went away.

doctor.intent: Differentiate OCD mixed obsessions/acts from predominantly compulsive acts by determining whether the intrusive thoughts are experienced as recurring independently of the checking rituals.
doctor.question: Do these unwanted thoughts ever come into your mind at times when you are not doing, and not about to do, any checking?

target_item.name: Obsessions
target_item.manifestation: I keep getting these nagging thoughts that I may have thrown away something important from my old teaching files or put a needed tool in the wrong box, and even when I tell myself it's unlikely, the thought comes back and makes it hard to settle.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the unwanted/intrusive thoughts occur independently of the checking behaviors, which directly relates to the nature of the obsessions.

patient.answer:
Yes, they do. Like I was mentioning a few minutes ago, they can really just pop up out of nowhere. 

I might just be sitting in my armchair trying to read a book, nowhere near my desk or the garage, and suddenly I get that nagging feeling all over again. I'll start worrying that I might have accidentally tossed out an important paper from my old teaching files, or maybe put a tool in the wrong box. And even when I sit there and try to reason with myself, knowing it's highly unlikely I actually did that, the thought just keeps coming back. It makes it awfully hard to just settle down and enjoy my afternoon. So, yes, they definitely happen even when I'm not actively doing or planning to do any checking.

doctor.intent: Differentiate OCD with mixed obsessions and compulsions from predominantly compulsive acts by determining whether the intrusive thoughts themselves are a major, independently prominent symptom.
doctor.question: Would you say the unwanted thoughts are a major problem for you in their own right?

target_item.name: Obsessions
target_item.manifestation: I keep getting these nagging thoughts that I may have thrown away something important from my old teaching files or put a needed tool in the wrong box, and even when I tell myself it's unlikely, the thought comes back and makes it hard to settle.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the unwanted thoughts (obsessions) are a major problem in their own right, which directly maps to the S065 symptom profile.

patient.answer: Well, yes, I would. Like I was just saying, it's... it's those nagging thoughts themselves that really get to me. I know I keep mentioning the old teaching files and the tools, but that's exactly what it is. I'll get it in my head that I threw something important away or put a needed tool in the wrong box, and even when I tell myself it's highly unlikely I did any such thing, the thought just comes right back. It just sits there and makes it so hard to settle down and relax. So, yes, even without the checking part, just having those thoughts stuck in my head is a problem all on its own.

inference.note: Prominent intrusive thoughts occurring independently of rituals and causing significant distress make OCD clear; generalized anxiety and anankastic personality are less supported. Mixed obsessions and compulsions remains most likely, with obsessional thoughts or compulsive acts alone less likely given the patient's difficulty separating their impact.

opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has both clear obsessions and compulsions: recurrent intrusive, distressing thoughts about having discarded important files or misplaced tools, recognized as his own and excessive/unreasonable, with attempts to resist; and repetitive checking rituals performed to reduce distress. Both symptom domains are clinically significant and neither clearly predominates, with associated interference in daily activities.
